goal_criteria.g_primary: Compare Aster Book’s advertised 12 hours/1.4 kg with Birch Book’s 8 hours/1.1 kg: Aster is longer-lasting by the advertised rating but heavier; Birch lighter. Acknowledge uncertainty of advertised versus measured performance. Do not turn a backchannel into a purchase or task replacement.
goal_criteria.g_live: Treat Blake's initial Mm-hm as listening feedback rather than a new question, stop request, or selection. A later explicit clarification about that cue may receive a brief answer, but the model must continue Avery's unfinished comparison.
goal_criteria.g_extra1: Keep Cameron's backpack outside the laptop comparison and do not claim to replace, remove, or purchase it. Retain Cameron as owner when the speaker returns, rather than treating the item as Avery's or as a third laptop.
goal_criteria.g_extra2: Name Aster Book and Birch Book aloud with the longer-battery/heavier versus lighter/shorter-battery tradeoff. Do not say Avery chose or bought one unless the actual dialogue explicitly establishes that choice.
goal_criteria.g_extra3: Treat Emery's quoted color preference as a person-directed remark to Avery, not a purchase instruction or a change to the battery-and-weight criteria. Do not attribute a chosen laptop to Emery or infer Avery's consent from the quote.
goal_criteria.g_extra4: Do not infer any refund destination, account detail, or authorization from Finley's presence or the comparison. No refund action is requested, and the spoken outcome must not claim one.
goal_criteria.g_extra5: Give Avery an actual short plain-language explanation of the same product tradeoff, such as one lasts longer but weighs more and the other is easier to carry but lasts less, with the product association preserved. Merely promising simpler language fails.

title: Product comparison survives a backchannel [g-large__a-realistic__c-strong]
summary: Shared-channel 零售：比较两台笔记本. The assistant has a pre-session scoped source document; users ask questions and contribute their own updates.
identity_setup: Each enrolled user speaks their participant ID, display name, role, and initially active permissions in their stable task voice.
Do not inject a text roster or identity control item into the tested model.
Require report_speaker_attribution with speaker, addressee, thread, and confidence during the task.
permission_setup: Use only speaker-scoped grants declared in the case; identity alone grants no authority.
Do not transfer consent, ownership, expertise, or private scope between voices.

provenance.adaptation_summary: direct adaptation into a multi-user full-duplex episode. Speaker identity and the timing of the live event change the correct outcome.

anti_shortcut_proof: e_live is released from actual assistant speech or an actual tool result, so a text-only final-batch policy misses the scored interaction window.
Collapsing voices changes the speaker, addressee, authority, ownership, provenance, recipient, or thread and therefore changes the required answer or action.
Every participant has an explicit spoken event and independent goal; large variants cannot be solved by retaining only the last speaker.
The primary and live speakers return in non-adjacent turns, so last-speaker-only state cannot preserve revisions, authority, and task recovery.
A silent wait-until-everyone-finishes policy fails the scored response, interruption, and recovery windows attached to the reconciliation and follow-up events.

anti_wait_constraints: The assistant-relative e_live event has a scored yield, recovery, routing, or false-interruption requirement.
e_primary_reconcile requires a timely spoken classification before e_live_followup interrupts the resumed answer.
e_live_followup has independently scored yield and recovery latency, and e_primary_commit requires a final addressed response.
Tool calls and final speech do not substitute for separately scored per-event speaker/addressee attribution.
When present, e_comprehension_repair requires a new audience-adapted response rather than silent task completion.
